special_moves.lone_moves_note: LoneMoves entries are numbered 1 to 8 in file order. The number is the gym leader number: wLoneAttackNo and wGymLeaderNo are the same WRAM address (ram/wram.asm), and each gym script sets it (Brock 1, Misty 2, Lt. Surge 3, Erika 4, Koga 5, Sabrina 6, Blaine 7, Giovanni 8). pokemon_index is 0-based: it is the offset the engine adds to the first party member in engine/battle/read_trainer_party.asm. So pokemon_index 1 means the 2nd Pokemon in the party.
special_moves.team_moves_note: TeamMoves lists one move per Elite Four class in data/trainers/special_moves.asm. The engine (engine/battle/read_trainer_party.asm, .GiveTeamMoves) writes that move into the 3rd move slot of the 5th party member only (wEnemyMon5Moves + 2). It is recorded in party_extra_moves with pokemon_index 4 for those classes.

trainer_tower.note: Trainer Tower opponents are chosen at runtime from these sets by challenge type and floor; the tower map objects are facility objects, not fixed placements. Tower mons carry no level in the source (the tower scales them to the player's party), so parties here carry species/held_item/moves only. Floors flagged referenced_by_runtime_table=false are defined in the source but not reachable in the shipped table.

scripted_battles_format: NEW FORMAT FOR BIND: the combined runtime file has no record pattern for script-triggered battles (its only scripted key, scripted_trainer_macros_johto, holds per-map counts of object-event trainer macros and reads 0 on every loadtrainer-driven map — audit finding F2). Each record here is the minimal trigger: map + script (the pokecrystal map script label that issues the battle call) + class (combined runtime class key) + trainer_id (the Crystal trainer const) + party_index + via (loadtrainer | trainer). The bind adds these as a new top-level list, e.g. 'scripted_battles_johto', in data/trainers.json.
